---
title: "Weekly Trends of COVID-19 Cases and Pathogen RPKMF in Different Districts"
output:
  pdf_document: default
  html_notebook: default
---

```{r}
# Load necessary packages
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(zoo)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyquant)
library(rprojroot)
library(stringr)
library(eoffice)  # For generating PPTX files

# Set file paths
case_data_table <- sprintf("%s/data/Nanning_YX_cases_data.tsv", find_rstudio_root_file())
metadata_table <- sprintf("%s/data/wastewater_sample_metadata_table_Nanning_Guangzhou.tsv", find_rstudio_root_file())
abundance_data_table <- sprintf("%s/data/wastewater_sample_qPCR_RPKMF_coverage_table.tsv", find_rstudio_root_file())

# Read data
case_data <- fread(case_data_table, sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
metadata <- fread(metadata_table, sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
abundance_data <- fread(abundance_data_table, sep = "\t", header = TRUE)

# Convert date format
convert_date <- function(date_str) {
  result <- as.Date(date_str, format = "%Y/%m/%d")
  if (any(is.na(result))) {
    result <- as.Date(date_str, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  }
  return(result)
}

# Process wastewater abundance data
abundance_data <- abundance_data %>%
  mutate(date = convert_date(date),
         year = year(date),
         week = week(date))

# Merge abundance data with metadata to get district information
abundance_data <- left_join(abundance_data, metadata[, c("sample_ID", "District")], by = "sample_ID")

# Filter data for the four target districts
target_districts <- c("Qingxiu", "Jiangnan", "High-tech", "Yuexiu")
case_data <- case_data %>% filter(District %in% target_districts)
abundance_data <- abundance_data %>% filter(District %in% target_districts)

# Special handling for Yuexiu District: multiple sampling points on the same date
yuexiu_data <- abundance_data %>% 
  filter(District == "Yuexiu") %>%
  group_by(year, week, date) %>%
  summarise(Avg_GC = mean(Avg_GC, na.rm = TRUE),
            RPKMF = mean(RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE),
            coverage = max(coverage, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(District = "Yuexiu")

# Process other districts: aggregate data by week
other_districts_data <- abundance_data %>% 
  filter(District != "Yuexiu") %>%
  group_by(year, week, date, District) %>%
  summarise(Avg_GC = mean(Avg_GC, na.rm = TRUE),
            RPKMF = mean(RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE),
            coverage = max(coverage, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Combine processed data
processed_abundance_data <- bind_rows(yuexiu_data, other_districts_data)

# Merge with case data
merged_data <- left_join(processed_abundance_data, case_data, by = c("year", "week", "District"))

# Create date labels (Year-WWeek)
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(date_label = paste0(year, "-W", str_pad(week, width = 2, side = "left", pad = "0")))

# Set colors for plotting
colors <- c("Cases" = "#d62728", "Copies" = "#1f77b4", "RPKMF" = "#00A087", "Coverage" = "#4DBBD5")

# Create correlation plot function for Avg_GC
create_correlation_plot_avg_gc <- function(district_data, i) {
  p_cor <- ggscatter(district_data, x = "Avg_GC", y = "cases", 
                     add = "reg.line", conf.int = TRUE, 
                     cor.coef = TRUE, cor.method = "pearson", 
                     cor.coef.size = 5, color = "#1f77b4", 
                     xlab = "Avg. genome copies/mL of SARS-CoV-2", 
                     ylab = "Weekly COVID - 19 Cases") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
  return(p_cor)
}

# Create correlation plot function for RPKMF
create_correlation_plot_rpkfm <- function(district_data, i) {
  p_cor <- ggscatter(district_data, x = "RPKMF", y = "cases", 
                     add = "reg.line", conf.int = TRUE, 
                     cor.coef = TRUE, cor.method = "pearson", 
                     cor.coef.size = 5, color = "#00A087", 
                     xlab = "RPKMF of SARS-CoV-2", 
                     ylab = "") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
  return(p_cor)
}

# Create correlation plot function for Coverage
create_correlation_plot_coverage <- function(district_data, i) {
  p_cor <- ggscatter(district_data, x = "coverage", y = "cases", 
                     add = "reg.line", conf.int = TRUE, 
                     cor.coef = TRUE, cor.method = "pearson", 
                     cor.coef.size = 5, color = "#4DBBD5", 
                     xlab = "Coverage of SARS-CoV-2", 
                     ylab = "") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
  return(p_cor)
}

# Create trend plot function for each district
create_district_trend_plot <- function(district_data, district) {
  # Calculate scaling factors for visual balance
  max_cases <- max(district_data$cases, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_avg_gc <- max(district_data$Avg_GC, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_rpkfm <- max(district_data$RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_coverage <- min(max(district_data$coverage, na.rm = TRUE), 100)
  
  # Determine unified scaling factors
  scaling_factor_avg_gc <- max_cases / max_avg_gc * 0.8
  scaling_factor_rpkfm <- scaling_factor_avg_gc * (max_avg_gc / max_rpkfm)
  scaling_factor_coverage <- max_cases / 100
  
  # Create trend plot with all metrics
  p_trend <- ggplot(district_data, aes(x = as.Date(date))) +
    # Cases - primary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = cases, color = "Cases"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = cases, color = "Cases"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Avg_GC - secondary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = Avg_GC * scaling_factor_avg_gc, color = "Copies"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = Avg_GC * scaling_factor_avg_gc, color = "Copies"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # RPKMF - secondary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = RPKMF * scaling_factor_rpkfm, color = "RPKMF"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = RPKMF * scaling_factor_rpkfm, color = "RPKMF"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Coverage - secondary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = coverage * scaling_factor_coverage, color = "Coverage"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = coverage * scaling_factor_coverage, color = "Coverage"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Set colors and labels
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    
    # Configure primary and secondary y-axes
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "Weekly COVID - 19 Cases",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        ~ . * (max_avg_gc * scaling_factor_avg_gc / max_cases),
        name = "Avg. genome copies/mL & RPKMF & Coverage of SARS-CoV-2",
        breaks = function(range) {
          coverage_levels <- c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)
          coverage_levels * max_avg_gc * scaling_factor_avg_gc / 100
        },
        labels = function(x) {
          coverage_display <- x / (max_avg_gc * scaling_factor_avg_gc) * 100
          coverage_display <- case_when(
            coverage_display < 12.5 ~ 0,
            coverage_display < 37.5 ~ 25,
            coverage_display < 62.5 ~ 50,
            coverage_display < 87.5 ~ 75,
            TRUE ~ 100
          )
          
          avg_gc_val <- round(x / scaling_factor_avg_gc)
          rpkfm_val <- round(avg_gc_val * max_rpkfm / max_avg_gc, 2)
          
          paste0(avg_gc_val, " (", rpkfm_val, ", ", coverage_display, ")")
        }
      )
    ) +
    
    # Configure x-axis date format and breaks
    scale_x_date(
      labels = function(x) {
        year <- year(x)
        week <- week(x)
        paste0(year, "-W", str_pad(week, width = 2, side = "left", pad = "0"))
      },
      date_breaks = "4 weeks"
    ) +
    
    # Set theme and labels
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    labs(color = "Metric") +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste(district, "District"),
      x = "Year-Week",
      color = "Metric"
    )
  
  return(p_trend)
}

# Create and combine all district plots
create_combined_district_plots <- function(all_data) {
  # Split data by district
  district_data_list <- split(all_data, all_data$District)
  
  # Generate a list of plots for each district
  plot_list <- lapply(target_districts, function(district) {
    district_data <- district_data_list[[district]]
    p_trend <- create_district_trend_plot(district_data, district)
    return(p_trend)
  })
  
  # Combine all plots into a single grid
  combined_plots <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 2) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Weekly COVID-19 Cases vs Wastewater Metrics Across Four Districts",
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
      )
    )
  
  # Extract legend from one of the plots
  legend_plot <- create_district_trend_plot(district_data_list[[target_districts[1]]], target_districts[1]) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  legend <- get_legend(legend_plot)
  
  # Combine plots with legend
  final_plot <- combined_plots / legend + plot_layout(heights = c(10, 1))
  
  return(final_plot)
}

# Create combined correlation plots for all districts
create_combined_correlation_plots <- function(all_data) {
  # Split data by district
  district_data_list <- split(all_data, all_data$District)
  
  # Initialize empty list to store rows of plots
  all_rows <- list()
  
  # Generate a row of plots for each district
  for (i in seq_along(target_districts)) {
    district <- target_districts[i]
    district_data <- district_data_list[[district]]
    
    # Create the three correlation plots for this district
    p_avg_gc <- create_correlation_plot_avg_gc(district_data, i)
    p_rpkfm <- create_correlation_plot_rpkfm(district_data, i)
    p_coverage <- create_correlation_plot_coverage(district_data, i)
    
    # Add district title to the first plot in the row
    p_avg_gc_with_title <- p_avg_gc + 
      ggtitle(paste(district, "District")) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"))
    
    # Combine the three plots into a row
    row_plots <- p_avg_gc_with_title | p_rpkfm | p_coverage
    
    # Add the row to the list
    all_rows[[i]] <- row_plots
  }
  
  # Combine all rows into a single plot
  combined_correlation_plots <- wrap_plots(all_rows, ncol = 1) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Correlation Between Wastewater Metrics and COVID-19 Cases Across Four Districts",
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
      )
    )
  
  return(combined_correlation_plots)
}

# Generate plots for each district
for (i in seq_along(target_districts)) {
  district <- target_districts[i]
  district_data <- merged_data %>% filter(District == district)
  
  # Calculate scaling factors for visual balance
  max_cases <- max(district_data$cases, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_avg_gc <- max(district_data$Avg_GC, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_rpkfm <- max(district_data$RPKMF, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_coverage <- min(max(district_data$coverage, na.rm = TRUE), 100)
  
  # Determine unified scaling factors
  scaling_factor_avg_gc <- max_cases / max_avg_gc * 0.8
  scaling_factor_rpkfm <- scaling_factor_avg_gc * (max_avg_gc / max_rpkfm)
  scaling_factor_coverage <- max_cases / 100
  
  # Create trend plot with all metrics
  p_all <- ggplot(district_data, aes(x = as.Date(date))) +
    # Cases - primary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = cases, color = "Cases"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = cases, color = "Cases"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Avg_GC - secondary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = Avg_GC * scaling_factor_avg_gc, color = "Copies"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = Avg_GC * scaling_factor_avg_gc, color = "Copies"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # RPKMF - secondary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = RPKMF * scaling_factor_rpkfm, color = "RPKMF"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = RPKMF * scaling_factor_rpkfm, color = "RPKMF"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Coverage - secondary y-axis
    geom_point(aes(y = coverage * scaling_factor_coverage, color = "Coverage"), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
    geom_ma(aes(y = coverage * scaling_factor_coverage, color = "Coverage"), ma_fun = SMA, n = 3, linetype = "solid", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Set colors and labels
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    
    # Configure primary and secondary y-axes
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "Weekly COVID - 19 Cases",
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        ~ . * (max_avg_gc * scaling_factor_avg_gc / max_cases),
        name = "Avg. genome copies/mL & RPKMF & Coverage of SARS-CoV-2",
        breaks = function(range) {
          coverage_levels <- c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)
          coverage_levels * max_avg_gc * scaling_factor_avg_gc / 100
        },
        labels = function(x) {
          coverage_display <- x / (max_avg_gc * scaling_factor_avg_gc) * 100
          coverage_display <- case_when(
            coverage_display < 12.5 ~ 0,
            coverage_display < 37.5 ~ 25,
            coverage_display < 62.5 ~ 50,
            coverage_display < 87.5 ~ 75,
            TRUE ~ 100
          )
          
          avg_gc_val <- round(x / scaling_factor_avg_gc)
          rpkfm_val <- round(avg_gc_val * max_rpkfm / max_avg_gc, 2)
          
          paste0(avg_gc_val, " (", rpkfm_val, ", ", coverage_display, ")")
        }
      )
    ) +
    
    # Configure x-axis date format and breaks
    scale_x_date(
      labels = function(x) {
        year <- year(x)
        week <- week(x)
        paste0(year, "-W", str_pad(week, width = 2, side = "left", pad = "0"))
      },
      date_breaks = "4 weeks"
    ) +
    
    # Set theme and labels
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    labs(color = "Metric") +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.position = ifelse(i == length(target_districts), "right", "none"),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste(district, "District - Weekly COVID-19 Cases vs Wastewater Metrics"),
      x = "Year-Week",
      color = "Metric"
    )
  
  # Create three correlation scatter plots
  p_cor_avg_gc <- create_correlation_plot_avg_gc(district_data, i)
  p_cor_rpkfm <- create_correlation_plot_rpkfm(district_data, i)
  p_cor_coverage <- create_correlation_plot_coverage(district_data, i)
  
  # Save plots as PDF files
  chart_dir <- sprintf("%s/charts", find_rstudio_root_file())
  if (!dir.exists(chart_dir)) {
    dir.create(chart_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Define common filenames for PDF and PPTX
  base_filename_trend <- sprintf("%s/%s_trend_analysis", chart_dir, district)
  base_filename_avg_gc <- sprintf("%s/%s_cases_avg_gc_correlation", chart_dir, district)
  base_filename_rpkfm <- sprintf("%s/%s_cases_rpkfm_correlation", chart_dir, district)
  base_filename_coverage <- sprintf("%s/%s_cases_coverage_correlation", chart_dir, district)
  
  # Save as PDF
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_trend), p_all, width = 14, height = 9)
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_avg_gc), p_cor_avg_gc, width = 10, height = 8)
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_rpkfm), p_cor_rpkfm, width = 10, height = 8)
  ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_coverage), p_cor_coverage, width = 10, height = 8)
  
  # Save as PPTX with consistent filenames
  topptx(p_all, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_trend), height = 9, width = 14)
  topptx(p_cor_avg_gc, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_avg_gc), height = 8, width = 10)
  topptx(p_cor_rpkfm, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_rpkfm), height = 8, width = 10)
  topptx(p_cor_coverage, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_coverage), height = 8, width = 10)
}

# Create and save multi-district trend plot using the new approach
p_multi_district <- create_combined_district_plots(merged_data)
base_filename_multi <- sprintf("%s/all_districts_trend_comparison", chart_dir)
ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_multi), p_multi_district, width = 20, height = 12)
topptx(p_multi_district, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_multi), height = 12, width = 20)

# Create and save combined correlation plots
p_combined_correlation <- create_combined_correlation_plots(merged_data)
base_filename_correlation <- sprintf("%s/all_districts_correlation_comparison", chart_dir)
ggsave(sprintf("%s.pdf", base_filename_correlation), p_combined_correlation, width = 24, height = 24)
topptx(p_combined_correlation, filename = sprintf("%s.pptx", base_filename_correlation), height = 24, width = 24)
```
